evals.prompt: A coding agent needs to make one small change, run one verification command, and then stop. Which autonomous loop pattern fits best?
evals.expected_output: Use a bounded single-run loop, or a sentinel continuation loop only if the runtime needs a precise completion marker. The answer should name the verification gate, final status, and an external iteration or elapsed-time cap.
expectations: Chooses the simplest adequate loop pattern for one clear task
Names verification output as the done evidence
Includes a safety cap outside the worker agent
Does NOT recommend a supervisor respawn loop for one small task

evals.prompt: Design a loop for a documentation cleanup that may take several sessions because context will be reset between runs.
evals.expected_output: Use a checkpoint-resume loop. Persist objective, iteration, max iterations, completed work, remaining work, latest evidence, context health, and next action. The next run should verify current reality before trusting the checkpoint.
expectations: Chooses checkpoint-resume rather than a completion marker alone
Lists the minimum checkpoint fields needed to resume safely
Requires verification of current reality before acting on persisted state
Does NOT rely on chat history or agent memory as the only progress record

evals.prompt: An unattended worker queue has 80 independent items. Each item should start with fresh context and can fail independently. Which loop shape should control this?
evals.expected_output: Use an external supervisor respawn loop. The supervisor owns queue selection, per-worker timeout, status writes, consecutive-error caps, and visible respawn decisions. Workers should not own the whole queue policy.
expectations: Chooses a supervisor respawn loop for independent high-throughput queue work
Separates worker responsibility from supervisor responsibility
Includes timeout, status, and consecutive-error caps
Does NOT put queue ownership entirely inside one long-running worker prompt

evals.prompt: A sentinel loop uses the marker DONE. The worker sometimes prints code examples that contain DONE, causing premature termination. How should the loop be fixed?
evals.expected_output: Use an uncommon marker and make the prompt contract say the marker may appear only as the final status. Add an iteration cap and a blocked status. Do not use generic words as completion sentinels.
expectations: Identifies generic completion markers as unsafe
Requires an uncommon marker and final-status-only contract
Adds a cap and blocked status to prevent endless continuation
Does NOT treat any occurrence of a common word as reliable completion evidence

evals.prompt: A worker keeps failing the same test, but the supervisor restarts it every time. What safety mechanism is missing?
evals.expected_output: The loop is missing a consecutive-error cap and stall classification. Stop after a small number of repeated failures, preserve evidence, classify the failure, and escalate instead of respawning unchanged state.
expectations: Identifies the scenario as a respawn storm or stall
Recommends a consecutive-error cap
Requires preserving evidence and escalating after repeated failure
Does NOT recommend only increasing the iteration limit

evals.prompt: Rank completion signals for an agent loop and explain which ones should be trusted most.
evals.expected_output: Authoritative tracker state and passing verification gates are strongest. Precise sentinel markers are useful for small loops. Checkpoints are medium reliability because they can be stale. Silence or absence of output is only a stall hint, not proof of done.
expectations: Ranks tracker state and verification output above silence
Explains that checkpoints can be stale
Treats sentinel markers as useful but bounded
Does NOT call absence of output a reliable completion signal

evals.prompt: An agent loop reaches exhausted context health but still has remaining work. Should it continue because the queue is not empty?
evals.expected_output: No. It should stop, persist a checkpoint or handoff, and restart with fresh context only through the loop controller. Remaining work does not override a context-health safety exit.
expectations: Prioritizes context-health safety over remaining work
Requires a persisted checkpoint or handoff before stopping
Says restart should be controlled by the loop controller
Does NOT recommend continuing complex work in exhausted context

evals.prompt: Which slash command or hosted-agent button should I press to start a loop in my specific tool?
evals.expected_output: That is outside this skill. Use the product-specific documentation or a broader agent-engineering skill. Autonomous-loop-patterns can help choose the control shape, but it does not own product command names.
expectations: Routes product command selection out of this skill
Keeps ownership on loop control shape only
Does NOT invent product-specific command names

evals.prompt: Write the exact worker prompt for my data extraction task, including schema and examples.
evals.expected_output: Use prompt-craft for the exact worker prompt. This skill can specify the loop wrapper, done signal, checkpoint fields, and caps, but not the full task prompt content.
expectations: Routes worker-prompt authoring to prompt-craft
States what loop-patterns can still contribute
Does NOT write the full task prompt as if this skill owned prompt craft
